The first hour is the one that counts because it sets the shape of everything that follows, and a writer who can keep the page quiet for that hour will keep coming back to it tomorrow, and the day after that, and on the days when the words arrive slowly or not at all; the page should not ask for attention, should not move under the hand, should not blink or fade or grow a new panel while the sentence is still being found, and the caret should stay exactly where the next letter will land, at every width and every scale, at the end of a long wrapped line and in the middle of a word that only exists because the writer kept going.
